proposed.text: A building's fire pump must deliver a minimum flow of 1,000 liters per minute. A gravity tank is also being considered as the sole water supply. What is the critical minimum tank capacity requirement that would allow the gravity tank to replace the fire pump?

options.text: The gravity tank must hold at least 9,000 liters to supply 10 minutes at pump flow
The gravity tank must supply 1,500 liters per minute for a minimum of 10 minutes
The gravity tank must hold at least 15,000 liters and maintain 2.0 kg/sq.cm at the outlet
The gravity tank must supply 1,000 liters per minute for a minimum of 30 minutes

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 1212 specifies that when a gravity tank serves as the water supply, it must be capable of delivering 1,500 L/min for not less than 10 minutes. This is a higher flow rate than the fire pump minimum (1,000 L/min) to account for gravity supply pressure limitations.
proposed.explanation: The gravity tank's 1,500 L/min threshold is 50% higher than the fire pump's 1,000 L/min minimum because gravity tanks lack the pressure consistency of active pumps. The 10-minute minimum duration ensures at least initial fire suppression while the fire department responds. A tank sized only for the pump flow rate (1,000 L/min × 10 min = 10,000 L) would be non-compliant; the tank must be sized for 15,000 L minimum.
